bio: As further proof that big things often come in small packages, watch this narrow nook make a regular out of you in no time. On busy Orchard Street, this neighborhood gem hides in plain sight, anchored by a kitchen that doesn’t even have a proper gas stove. Seasonal, bright and unfussy, the menu is small but endlessly tempting as it roams the Middle East for inspiration. Simple, familiar things like tabbouleh chock full of fresh mint and sweet corn spark instant summer joy. Order anything with lamb, whether it’s wrapped in soft cabbage leaves or stuffed into squash blossoms, delicately fried and paired with creamy tzatziki. A punky soundtrack, a natural wine list and staff that will never judge you for over-ordering — what’s not to love?...
